arxiv-1705-04296.title: Displayed categories
arxiv-1705-04296.creator: Benedikt Ahrens, Peter LeFanu Lumsdaine
arxiv-1705-04296.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Benedikt Ahrens, Peter LeFanu Lumsdaine. We introduce and develop the notion of displayed categories . A displayed category over a category 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} is equivalent to ‘a category 𝒟 \mathcal{D} and functor F : 𝒟 → 𝒞 F:\mathcal{D}\to{\mathcal{C}} ’, but instead of having a single collection of ‘objects of 𝒟 \mathcal{D} ’ with a map to the objects of 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} , the objects are given as a family indexed by objects of 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} , and similarly for the morphisms.

arxiv-1804-08302.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by B. Ruf a,b, L. Thiel a, M. Weinmann b. With the technological advancements of aerial imagery and accurate 3d reconstruction of urban environments, more and more attention has been paid to the automated analyses of urban areas. In our work, we examine two important aspects that allow online analysis of building structures in city models given oblique aerial image sequences, namely automatic building extraction with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and selective real-time depth estimation from aerial imagery.

Dove prisms and K-mirrors are devices extensively used for rotating the wavefront of an optical field. These devices have several applications, including measurement of orbital angular momentum, microscopy, beam steering and pattern recognition. However, the wavefront rotation achieved through these devices is always accompanied by polarization changes in the incident field, which is an undesirable feature in many of these applications.

Subsequence Dynamic Time Warping (sDTW) is the metric of choice when performing many sequence matching and alignment tasks.
